headline: Traffic signs, Amoskeag Bridge detour, Maple Street lane change, and kratom ban to be discussed.
summary: The committee will review proposed stop signs, parking restrictions, and a crosswalk, plus a detour plan for the Amoskeag Bridge rehabilitation, a lane change on Maple Street, and an ordinance to ban kratom.
items: Traffic Division requests covering: stop sign at Ash Street and Webster Street (NE corner); no commercial vehicles on Allen Street between Boynton Street and S Main Street; no parking anytime on Jewett Street and S Jewett Street near Cilley Road; crosswalk on Park Side Avenue south of Putnam Street; rescind no parking November 15 - April 15 on Orange Street between Chestnut Street and Pine Street (ORD 9457)
Request from Jemco Properties LLC to install no parking signs in the new Karatzas Heights subdivision off Karatzas Avenue

Request from Caleb Dobbins, Highway Chief Engineer, for a detour route during the Amoskeag Bridge westbound rehabilitation project (2028/2029), keeping eastbound traffic on the eastbound bridge and detouring westbound traffic over the Bridge Street Bridge, with pedestrian/bicycle access on the second eastbound lane

Request from the Highway Chief Engineer to limit Maple Street from Hanover Street to Bridge Street to a single northbound lane, rescind no parking anytime on Maple Street west side from Cilley Road to Webster Street (ORD 3355), and add no parking anytime on Maple Street west side from Cilley Road to Hanover Street and from a point 60 feet north of Concord Street to Webster Street
Request from Aldermen Thomas and Barry for an Ordinance Amendment banning kratom

COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC SAFETY, HEALTH & TRAFFIC 
October 6, 2026 at 5:30 PM 
Aldermanic Chambers, City Hall (3rd Floor) 
 
Members: Aldermen Vincent, Goonan, Dexter, Barry, Bonilla 
 
AGENDA 
 
 
The Chairman calls the meeting to order. 
  
The Clerk calls the roll. 
  
1. The Traffic Division has submitted an agenda which needs to be addressed: 
STOP SIGN 
On Ash Street at Webster Street, NE corner 
Alderman Goonan 
NO COMMERCIAL VEHICLES 
On Allen Street, between Boynton Street and S Main Street 
Alderman Barry 
NO PARKING ANYTIME 
On Jewett Street, west side, from Cilley Road to a point 140 feet north 
On S Jewett Street, west side, from Cilley Road to a point 120 feet south 
On S Jewett Street, east side, from Cilley Road to a point 120 feet south 
Alderman Terrio 
CROSSWALK 
On Park Side Avenue, south of Putnam Street 
Alderman Vincent 
RESCIND NO PARKING NOVEMBER 15 - APRIL 15 
On Orange Street, south side, from Chestnut Street to Pine Street (ORD 9457) 
Alderman Dexter 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
2. Communication from Jemco Properties LLC, requesting approval to install no 
parking signs in the new Karatzas Heights subdivision extending off of Karatzas 
Avenue. 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure?
October 6, 2026 COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC SAFETY, HEALTH & TRAFFIC 
Page 2 of 2 
 
 
3. Communication from Caleb Dobbins, Highway Chief Engineer, requesting 
approval of the following detour route for the Amoskeag Bridge westbound 
rehabilitation project scheduled for 2028/2029: 
• Maintain eastbound traffic on eastbound bridge (single lane), detour 
westbound traffic over Bridge Street Bridge 
• Allow pedestrian/bicycle traffic to utilize the second lane (northern) on 
eastbound bridge 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
4. Communication from the Highway Chief Engineer requesting that Maple Street, 
from Hanover Street to Bridge Street, be limited to a single lane northbound, 
and that the following Traffic Ordinances be enacted: 
RESCIND NO PARKING ANYTIME 
On Maple Street, west side, from Cilley Road to Webster Street (ORD 3355) 
NO PARKING ANYTIME 
On Maple Street, west side, from Cilley Road to Hanover Street 
On Maple Street, west side, from a point 60 feet north of Concord Street to 
Webster Street 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
5. Communication from Aldermen Thomas and Barry requesting approval of an 
Ordinance Amendment banning the substance known as kratom. 
If the Committee so desires, a motion is in order that the Ordinance 
Amendment ought to pass and be referred to the Committee on Bills on 
Second Reading for technical review. 
    
If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn.
